en: Proverbs 17

p.src: 1  Better is a dry morsel with quietness, than a house full of feasting with strife.

en: Better is a dry morsel with quietness, than a house full of feasting with strife.
u.src: 1  Better is a dry morsel with quietness, than a house full of feasting with strife.

p.src: 2  A servant who deals wisely will rule over a son who causes shame, and shall have a part in the inheritance among the brothers.

en: A servant who deals wisely will rule over a son who causes shame, and shall have a part in the inheritance among the brothers.
u.src: 2  A servant who deals wisely will rule over a son who causes shame, and shall have a part in the inheritance among the brothers.

p.src: 3  The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold, but the LORD tests the hearts.

en: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold, but the LORD tests the hearts.
u.src: 3  The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold, but the LORD tests the hearts.

p.src: 4  An evildoer heeds wicked lips. A liar gives ear to a mischievous tongue.

en: An evildoer heeds wicked lips. A liar gives ear to a mischievous tongue.
u.src: 4  An evildoer heeds wicked lips. A liar gives ear to a mischievous tongue.

p.src: 5  Whoever mocks the poor reproaches his Maker. He who is glad at calamity shall not be unpunished.

en: Whoever mocks the poor reproaches his Maker. He who is glad at calamity shall not be unpunished.
u.src: 5  Whoever mocks the poor reproaches his Maker. He who is glad at calamity shall not be unpunished.

p.src: 6  Children’s children are the crown of old men; the glory of children is their parents.

en: Children’s children are the crown of old men; the glory of children is their parents.
u.src: 6  Children’s children are the crown of old men; the glory of children is their parents.

p.src: 7  Excellent speech isn’t fitting for a fool, much less do lying lips fit a prince.

en: Excellent speech isn’t fitting for a fool, much less do lying lips fit a prince.
u.src: 7  Excellent speech isn’t fitting for a fool, much less do lying lips fit a prince.

p.src: 8  A bribe is a precious stone in the eyes of him who gives it; wherever he turns, he prospers.

en: A bribe is a precious stone in the eyes of him who gives it; wherever he turns, he prospers.
u.src: 8  A bribe is a precious stone in the eyes of him who gives it; wherever he turns, he prospers.

p.src: 9  He who covers an offense promotes love; but he who repeats a matter separates best friends.

en: He who covers an offense promotes love; but he who repeats a matter separates best friends.
u.src: 9  He who covers an offense promotes love; but he who repeats a matter separates best friends.

p.src: 10  A rebuke enters deeper into one who has understanding than a hundred lashes into a fool.

en: A rebuke enters deeper into one who has understanding than a hundred lashes into a fool.
u.src: 10  A rebuke enters deeper into one who has understanding than a hundred lashes into a fool.

p.src: 11  An evil man seeks only rebellion; therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.

en: An evil man seeks only rebellion; therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.
u.src: 11  An evil man seeks only rebellion; therefore a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.

p.src: 12  Let a bear robbed of her cubs meet a man, rather than a fool in his folly.

en: Let a bear robbed of her cubs meet a man, rather than a fool in his folly.
u.src: 12  Let a bear robbed of her cubs meet a man, rather than a fool in his folly.

p.src: 13  Whoever rewards evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.

en: Whoever rewards evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.
u.src: 13  Whoever rewards evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.

p.src: 14  The beginning of strife is like breaching a dam, therefore stop contention before quarreling breaks out.

en: The beginning of strife is like breaching a dam, therefore stop contention before quarreling breaks out.
u.src: 14  The beginning of strife is like breaching a dam, therefore stop contention before quarreling breaks out.

p.src: 15  He who justifies the wicked, and he who condemns the righteous, both of them alike are an abomination to the LORD.

en: He who justifies the wicked, and he who condemns the righteous, both of them alike are an abomination to the LORD.
u.src: 15  He who justifies the wicked, and he who condemns the righteous, both of them alike are an abomination to the LORD.

p.src: 16  Why is there money in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, since he has no understanding?

en: Why is there money in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, since he has no understanding?
u.src: 16  Why is there money in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, since he has no understanding?

p.src: 17  A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.

en: A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.
u.src: 17  A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.

p.src: 18  A man void of understanding strikes hands, and becomes collateral in the presence of his neighbor.

en: A man void of understanding strikes hands, and becomes collateral in the presence of his neighbor.
u.src: 18  A man void of understanding strikes hands, and becomes collateral in the presence of his neighbor.

p.src: 19  He who loves disobedience loves strife. One who builds a high gate seeks destruction.

en: He who loves disobedience loves strife. One who builds a high gate seeks destruction.
u.src: 19  He who loves disobedience loves strife. One who builds a high gate seeks destruction.

p.src: 20  One who has a perverse heart doesn’t find prosperity, and one who has a deceitful tongue falls into trouble.

en: One who has a perverse heart doesn’t find prosperity, and one who has a deceitful tongue falls into trouble.
u.src: 20  One who has a perverse heart doesn’t find prosperity, and one who has a deceitful tongue falls into trouble.

p.src: 21  He who becomes the father of a fool grieves. The father of a fool has no joy.

en: He who becomes the father of a fool grieves. The father of a fool has no joy.
u.src: 21  He who becomes the father of a fool grieves. The father of a fool has no joy.

p.src: 22  A cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.

en: A cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.
u.src: 22  A cheerful heart makes good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones.

p.src: 23  A wicked man receives a bribe in secret, to pervert the ways of justice.

en: A wicked man receives a bribe in secret, to pervert the ways of justice.
u.src: 23  A wicked man receives a bribe in secret, to pervert the ways of justice.

p.src: 24  Wisdom is before the face of one who has understanding, but the eyes of a fool wander to the ends of the earth.

en: Wisdom is before the face of one who has understanding, but the eyes of a fool wander to the ends of the earth.
u.src: 24  Wisdom is before the face of one who has understanding, but the eyes of a fool wander to the ends of the earth.

p.src: 25  A foolish son brings grief to his father, and bitterness to her who bore him.

en: A foolish son brings grief to his father, and bitterness to her who bore him.
u.src: 25  A foolish son brings grief to his father, and bitterness to her who bore him.

p.src: 26  Also to punish the righteous is not good, nor to flog officials for their integrity.

en: Also to punish the righteous is not good, nor to flog officials for their integrity.
u.src: 26  Also to punish the righteous is not good, nor to flog officials for their integrity.

p.src: 27  He who spares his words has knowledge. He who is even tempered is a man of understanding.

en: He who spares his words has knowledge. He who is even tempered is a man of understanding.
u.src: 27  He who spares his words has knowledge. He who is even tempered is a man of understanding.

p.src: 28  Even a fool, when he keeps silent, is counted wise. When he shuts his lips, he is thought to be discerning.

en: Even a fool, when he keeps silent, is counted wise. When he shuts his lips, he is thought to be discerning.
u.src: 28  Even a fool, when he keeps silent, is counted wise. When he shuts his lips, he is thought to be discerning.
